name: REC Alpha Pure-R 400W
notes: Technology: HJT (heterojunction) cells, 80 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, lead-free construction. Runs 400-430W in 10W steps. Pros: HJT's best-in-class temperature coefficient and lowest degradation of any silicon technology, plus a unique 4-section cell layout for shading tolerance; notably high voltage (58.9-59.7V) and low current (under 9A) suit longer strings than a typical panel of this wattage. Cons: among the most expensive technologies per watt on the market alongside Maxeon's IBC, and monofacial only despite HJT's naturally high bifaciality potential.

name: REC Alpha Pure-RX 450W
notes: Technology: HJT (heterojunction) cells, 88 half-cut, gapless cell layout, single 3.2mm front glass with a black polymer backsheet. Runs 450-475W in 5W steps - REC's most powerful residential panel. Pros: an exceptionally high power density (up to 228 W/m2) keeps the panel physically compact for its wattage, and current stays under 9A across the range for straightforward MLPE/MPPT compatibility. Cons: despite REC's own datasheet describing the cells themselves as bifacial, the opaque black backsheet means this specific module is sold and specified as monofacial - there's no rear-side yield here, unlike the true bifacial Alpha Pure-R; it's also one of REC's most expensive panels per unit.
